subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` become isolated-writable across workspace mounts, filesystem bridges, browser/remote backends, and tool exposure, while preserving real-workspace isolation and protected skill/read-only bind boundaries?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the fix intentionally changes sandbox write permissions and must reflect maintainer security intent rather than an automated cleanup guess.

options.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
options.body: Implement writable `/workspace` only for the per-sandbox workspace, keep the real agent workspace unmounted, and update local/remote/browser bridges, tool exposure, docs, tests, and live proof together.

options.title: Keep None Read-Only
options.body: Document `none` as a no-write sandbox mode, hide write-capable tools consistently, and close this issue as not planned.

options.title: Defer To Broader Bind Policy
options.body: Keep this issue blocked until maintainers jointly decide isolated workspace writes and writable custom bind semantics with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718.

recommendation.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
recommendation.body: Implement writable `/workspace` only for the per-sandbox workspace, keep the real agent workspace unmounted, and update local/remote/browser bridges, tool exposure, docs, tests, and live proof together.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest workspaceAccess history and provided the latest maintainer direction that this issue remains the canonical fix path.
